answer: Payouts can ramp with tenure: an agent's share starts near its nadir and climbs only while an unbroken thread of graded epochs, each judged by a randomly drawn panel, stays intact. One missed or failed epoch resets the ramp. A farm of aliases cannot ride a single rising tide; every fake must sustain its own months-long chain of independently reviewed work, so the cost of an attack grows linearly with every identity added.
